title: Notes on a Musical Staff
description: Read the basic page symbols used to place a melody on five lines.
cardDescription: Read the basic page symbols used to place a melody on five lines.
focus: The staff locates pitches; a clef gives those lines and spaces their note-name reference.
solvingTip: Start with the shapes visible on the printed page.
words: Set of five parallel lines used for musical notation
Symbol setting the pitch reference of a musical staff
Word before clef for the familiar curled G-clef symbol
Word before line for a short extra line beyond the staff
Gap between two neighboring staff lines
One of the five parallel marks in a staff
Symbol representing a musical sound and its duration
Thin upright stroke attached to many printed notes
Oval part of a printed musical note
Word before clef for the symbol often used for low notes
Symbol that raises a written note by a semitone
Symbol that lowers a written note by a semitone
Symbol canceling a written sharp or flat
How high or low a written note sounds

answerNotes.STAFF: Notes can be placed on lines or in the spaces between them.
answerNotes.CLEF: A clef gives meaning to note positions rather than setting the tempo.
answerNotes.TREBLE: Treble clef places G on the second line of the staff.
answerNotes.LEDGER: Ledger lines extend notation above or below the five main lines.
answerNotes.SPACE: A note in a space has a different position from a note on a line.

title: Counting a Simple Musical Beat
description: Follow note lengths, silent rests, and the steady pulse beneath a familiar tune.
cardDescription: Follow note lengths, silent rests, and the steady pulse beneath a familiar tune.
focus: In common four-four counting, a quarter note often represents one beat; other meters use different conventions.
solvingTip: Use counting words before the printed notation terms.
words: Steady underlying beat felt in a piece of music
Note value often counted as one beat in four-four time
Note value half as long as a quarter note
Symbol marking a period of musical silence
Device clicking or marking a steady practice beat
Note value lasting twice as long as a quarter note
Note value lasting four quarter-note durations
Mark adding half the original value to a note's duration
Thick line joining the stems of short note values
Say numbers to keep track of a musical pulse
At a low speed, as a practice tempo may begin
At a high speed, as a lively tempo may be
Mark a steady pulse with a finger or foot
One regular pulse unit in the music

answerNotes.PULSE: A pulse is the regular reference, while rhythms can move across it.
answerNotes.QUARTER: The count depends on the meter; a quarter note is not always one beat.
answerNotes.EIGHTH: Two eighth notes equal one quarter note in written duration.
answerNotes.REST: A rest has a duration just as a sounded note does.
answerNotes.METRONOME: A metronome supplies a reference pulse, not the melody.

title: High and Low Notes at the Piano
description: Compare high and low sounds through ordinary directions, a keyboard, and a familiar melody.
cardDescription: Compare high and low sounds through ordinary directions, a keyboard, and a familiar melody.
subtheme: High and Low Notes at the Piano
focus: The clues describe pitch with everyday words rather than detailed scale formulas.
solvingTip: Start with a direction, body part, or movement word.
words: Describing a pitch near the upper end of a piano
Single pitched sound played on the piano
Sequence of musical notes going up or down
Keyboard instrument used to compare the pitches
White or black lever pressed to sound a piano note
Small movement from one musical note to the next
Body part whose fingers play the keyboard
Body part used to compare the two sounds
Produce a tune with the voice
Melody played in the little piano exercise
Keyboard direction toward the lower notes
Keyboard direction toward the higher notes

answerNotes.HIGH: High describes pitch here rather than loudness.
answerNotes.LOW: Low describes pitch rather than a quiet volume.
answerNotes.NOTE: A note has a pitch that can be compared with another note.
answerNotes.SCALE: A scale is a sequence rather than several notes all sounded together.
answerNotes.PIANO: A piano's keys can produce both higher and lower sounds.

title: Loud and Soft Sounds Around a Song
description: Compare a whisper, hum, bell, and drum through simple words for the sounds we hear.
cardDescription: Compare a whisper, hum, bell, and drum through simple words for the sounds we hear.
subtheme: Loud and Soft Sounds Around a Song
focus: The clues use everyday sound and voice words rather than Italian performance directions.
solvingTip: Try the short action words before the sound descriptions.
words: Strong in volume, as a forceful sound is
Quiet in volume, as a gentle sung passage is
Speak very quietly with a breathy voice
Call out in a very loud voice
Make a tune with the lips closed
Quality or character of a musical sound
Human sound used to speak or sing
Perceive a song with the ears
Carry words and melody with the voice
Metal object producing a ringing sound
Percussion instrument struck to make a beat
Make a light short striking sound

answerNotes.LOUD: Loudness describes sound level rather than musical pitch.
answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes the volume in this sound scene rather than a fabric texture.
answerNotes.WHISPER: A whisper is quiet speech rather than a normal full singing tone.
answerNotes.SHOUT: Shouting increases the strength of the voice rather than naming a musical note.
answerNotes.HUM: Humming produces a melody without clearly spoken words.

title: Following a Song on the Printed Page
description: Read a familiar song through its title, notes, words, and simple page-turning directions.
cardDescription: Read a familiar song through its title, notes, words, and simple page-turning directions.
subtheme: Following a Song on the Printed Page
focus: A score is written music. These clues focus on ordinary parts of the page rather than specialized repeat symbols.
solvingTip: Begin with a reading action or a short printed-page word.
words: One printed side followed while singing the song
Written music used to follow the song

Musical work followed on the printed sheet

Final point of the written song

Look at the printed words and notes to understand them

answerNotes.PAGE: A page can hold words, musical notes, or both.
answerNotes.SCORE: Score names the printed musical notation rather than game points here.
answerNotes.VERSE: A verse can advance a story while the melody repeats.
answerNotes.REPEAT: Repeat is an ordinary action word rather than one specific printed symbol.
answerNotes.TITLE: A title identifies the work rather than a performance direction.
